pr_title: drivers: serial: uart_ns16550: add missing isr locking
pr_body:
ISR locking was missing in the UART driver for x86_64. This PR adds a spinlock mechanism to interrupt related services in the driver.

Fixes #23026

Now commentary: 16550 emulation in QEMU is known to have artifact, or better say, defects. Given that qemu_x86 is everyone's default testing target, I'm always on alert that some change may break interrupt-driven uart support in qemu_x86.

issue_context.title: missing ISR locking in UART driver?
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

When IO APIC working in fixed delivery mode to broadcast interrupts to all CPUs in SMP system, seems the UART may not work properly.

Running this app and will see that the console is not able to echo keyboard input.
$ west build -b qemu_x86_64 samples/subsys/console/echo/ && west build -t run

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Apply these commits:.
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/22848/commits/3a447e65a68d59581dede00d402b2e534aac417f
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/22848/commits/3ee41f80b55ebe766e2627286f270efc50ea878c

2. replace IOAPIC_LOWEST with IOAPIC_FIXED in drivers/interrupt_controller/intc_ioapic.c to make sure IO APIC is working in logical + fixed mode.

3. Run the test and it won't work.
$ west build -b qemu_x86_64 samples/subsys/console/echo/ && west build -t run

**Expected behavior**

Skip (2) and use IOAPIC_LOWEST to deliver IO APIC to one CPU only, and run the same test, the console will print whatever characters you input from keyboard.

This problem could be caused by UART driver doesn't have ISR locking, so that it will have problems if same interrupt is delivered to all CPUs.

@ZideChen0 Will this issue be resolved by your PR #23325?
From that description, it sounds like the patch yields successfully running samples/subsys/console/echo (test UART driver) on qemu_x86_64 (xapic, SP and SMP).

> @ZideChen0 Will this issue be resolved by your PR #23325?
> From that description, it sounds like the patch yields successfully running samples/subsys/console/echo (test UART driver) on qemu_x86_64 (xapic, SP and SMP).

Yes, with PR #23325, UART interrupt is supposed to be delivered to one CPU, so no ISR locking is needed.

@ZideChen0 I will try your PR, too, but saw that it does not touch the uart driver itself. So I created a Draft PR of changes that might be needed to the uart driver in addition. But I still have the issue described here with my patch #23026 (WIP) so I can get feedback as it relates to this issue.

We are taking different approaches to address this issue. In my patches, I configured UART interrupts as lowest priority delivery mode, so it's delivered to one CPU only, and no need to modify UART driver. For example: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/23325/commits/ab9d571aa7bb56a1891c93ed769fa421c39988cd#diff-5e7cae5167b76f9e0a04173995540696R65

In your PR, I think you are trying to add the spinlock, so even if same interrupt is delivered to multiple CPUs, it still can be correctly processed.

It seems to me, in the following cases, the spinlock doesn't have a chance to be released, thus the subsequent calls fail to grab the spinlock. In this particular use case (console/echo app), it seems driver/console/uart_console.c is a better place to add the spinlock, but this could impact all other UART drivers, and other UART use cases, like bluetooth is not taken care of ... so I don't know what is the best way to patch the UART driver.

fwiw At first I was a little unsure if we should use goto due to secure coding practice guidelines, but in this context looks like we are ok. At least according to MISRA-C which advises against the use of goto (Rule 15.1) but sets requirements if goto is put into use: 
Rule 15.2 (Required): The goto statement shall jump to a label declared later in the same function
Rule 15.3 (Required): Any label referenced by a goto statement shall be declared in the same block, or in any block enclosing the goto statement
